action.question: Which waveform style reads as 'real SPY' to you?

questions.question: Which waveform style reads as 'real SPY' to you?

options.label: B — clustering
options.description: GARCH-like. Quiet stretches and jittery stretches. Best general 'real SPY' match.

options.label: C — clustering + jumps
options.description: B plus rare sharp down-jumps. Most dramatic; reads like SPY during a correction.

options.label: A — plain GBM
options.description: Constant-vol random walk. Uniform jaggedness everywhere.

options.label: D — mean-reverting
options.description: Hovers near 40%. Less drift, more time near the band edge.

questions.question: Should I switch the demo charts from weekly to daily resolution?

options.label: Yes, switch to daily
options.description: Re-label scenes 4-7 as days (~125 trading days for band, ~270 for force). Daily resolution is what makes the noise look like a real chart.

options.label: Keep weekly
options.description: Stay at W1-W24/W36 labels and just apply noisier data. (Note: weekly real-SPY series IS smoother than daily — won't look as 'real').

Open this in a browser to preview:

`demos/rebalancing-waveform-preview.html`

(or `file:///Users/claudio1/dev/dstrader/.claude/worktrees/bridge-cse_0126VVcisWhjfbeGrKE2NAYY/demos/rebalancing-waveform-preview.html`)

You'll see four candidates side-by-side, each a 125-day (~6mo) SPY weight series drawn against the same ±5% band:

- **A — Plain GBM**: constant-vol random walk. Noisy but uniformly noisy.
- **B — GBM + volatility clustering**: GARCH-like; calm vs jittery stretches. Closest match to real SPY's "quiet, then noisy" rhythm.
- **C — Clustering + jumps**: B plus rare negative jumps. Adds the sharp down-spikes real SPY shows during corrections.
- **D — Mean-reverting + clustering**: hovers near 40% target — useful if you want a path that lingers around the band edge.
